issues: Dolphin is rendered as a noisy dithered/stippled pixel cloud with internal gaps rather than a solid lit-phosphor body; the head and pectoral fin read as scattered dots instead of a defined silhouette, and there is no clear rim light.
Loose pixel debris floating below the dolphin reads as random static/noise, not as a clean directional persistence trail or a water splash, breaking the organic illusion.
Dolphin occupies too little of the frame; wide empty black margins above and around it weaken its role as the absolute centerpiece.
Bottom FFT bar graph is too bright and high-contrast (near-white blocks), pulling the eye downward and competing with the dolphin.
Glow/bloom on the dolphin is too weak and flat — it looks like a stipple pattern printed on black rather than a glowing phosphor object with a soft halo.
Extra right-side metadata text (82BPM, PHR 24/32, etc.) adds clutter not present in the reference layout and brightens the lower-right corner.
suggestions: Rebuild the dolphin as a filled, smoothly-edged lit-phosphor silhouette with a brighter rim-light outline and a subtly dimmer interior, removing most of the dither noise so the body, dorsal fin, tail fluke and pectoral fin read as one continuous creature.
Scale the dolphin up to fill roughly 55-60% of the 128px height and recenter it so it visually dominates the panel and the empty margins shrink.
Replace the random sub-dolphin pixel scatter with a short, arc-following persistence trail (a few fading ghost frames behind the tail/body) so motion reads as clean afterglow, not fog or static.
Drop the FFT bars to a dimmer phosphor tone and reduce their peak height/contrast so the spectrum stays a quiet background element at the bottom.
Add a gentle, tight bloom halo around the dolphin's lit edges to achieve the OEL 'lit object' look without blowing out the silhouette or washing the black field.
Make the 2-3 water-surface lines even thinner and lower-contrast, and remove or dim the right-side metadata so the eye path stays dolphin -> top text -> waves -> FFT.
